info.bio:
There are at least two bands with this name, none of which are to be mistaken for The Runaways.

1. A punk band from Calgary, AB and surrounding areas:
http://wearenottherunaways.bandcamp.com
http://effusionrecords.tumblr.com

2. British Downtempo Hip-Hop producers A.J. Kwame and Joe 2 Grand. Formerly known as RPM under which name they released singles on Mo Wax. In 1995 they changed their name to the Runaways (also known as Runaways UK) and were signed to Ultimate Dilemma in the UK and Three Sixty Records in the US.

scenes.name: Decadencia y glam-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El rock siempre tuvo un elemento de decadencia, amoralidad y obscenidad; entre los Cockettes (1968) y el Rocky Horror Picture Show (1974) se convierte en producto de masas. Gran Bretaña lo llama glam-rock: T.Rex lo inaugura y lo casa con el hard rock; David Bowie lo lleva a su cima comercial convirtiendo el marketing en arte (Ziggy Stardust, la trilogía berlinesa con Eno). En EE UU, Alice Cooper, Sparks, Iggy Pop y Lou Reed (Berlin, Metal Machine Music, New York). El glam y la decadencia preparan el punk: Mott The Hoople, Be Bop Deluxe, New York Dolls, Heartbreakers, Dictators, Modern Lovers de Jonathan Richman, Runaways.

podcast.title: Formation and Inspiration (1975)
podcast.body: The Runaways were formed by producer Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the success of the all-female band Fanny. Active from 1975 to 1979, they are arguably recognized as the first all-female hard rock band, featuring future stars Joan Jett and Lita Ford. "The first is to a weirdo producer named Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the group to form the Runaways, arguably the first all-female hard rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: All-Female Los Angeles Band
podcast.body: The Runaways were an all-female band from Los Angeles, famously covered by Bratmobile with their song "Cherry Bomb." They represent an earlier wave of female-fronted rock that influenced later bands like the Riot Grrrl groups. "the all-female band from Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Career Trajectory and Japanese Success
podcast.body: Active from 1975 to 1979, The Runaways struggled to establish a significant career in North America but became a sensation in Japan, where they were highly successful and even recorded a live album in 1977. "During the four years they were together between 1975 and 1979, they really never had much of a career in North America. But in Japan, it's another story. They were quite the sensation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chainsaw Wood Carving Hobby
podcast.body: Cherie Currie, formerly of The Runaways, now dedicates her time to carving objects out of wood using a chainsaw. "Her thing is now carving things out of wood using a chainsaw."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Experiences with Sexism and Abuse
podcast.body: The band faced tremendous sexism, with legendary accounts suggesting that Fowley even had their crew throw objects at them during rehearsals to desensitize them to potential abuse during live performances. "Legend has it that Fowley had their crew throw stuff at them during rehearsals, so they get used to the abuse whenever they played live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First All-Female Hard Rock Band with International Attention
podcast.body: The Runaways, anchored by 15-year-old Sandy West on drums, are identified as the first all-female hard rock band in history to gain international attention. The group featured future stars like Joan Jett, Lita Ford, and Mickey Steele, along with Cherie Currie and Jackie Fox. "We can safely call them the first all-female hard rock band in history to receive international attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and International Popularity
podcast.body: The Runaways were a band composed of teenage girls, formed in 1975. While they were never very popular in the United States, they achieved significant popularity in Japan. "The runaways was a band made up of teenage girls and that band was formed in 1975. They were never very popular in the United States. They were very popular in Japan, though."

podcast.title: Formation and Pioneering Hard Rock
podcast.body: The Runaways were formed by producer Kim Fowley, who was reportedly inspired by the band Fanny. They are often considered the first all-female hard rock band, featuring notable members like Joan Jett and Lita Ford. "The first is to a weirdo producer named Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the group to form the Runaways, arguably the first all-female hard rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lasting Influence
podcast.body: The Runaways are now recognized as immensely important figures, particularly for inspiring subsequent generations of women in music, including bands in the LA punk scene like The Go-Go's, who started as a punk band and might not have existed without The Runaways' pioneering efforts. "Today, we look back at the Runaways as insanely important figures, especially to the generation of women that followed, including those in the LA punk scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mismanagement and Industry Sexism
podcast.body: The Runaways faced significant challenges due to poor management and marketing, including controversial advertising slogans like "Jailbait on the run." The prevailing sexist attitude that "girls couldn't rock" ultimately contributed to their downfall, alongside internal issues and drug problems. "Unfortunately, The Runaways were managed and marketed badly. Jailbait on the run was one advertising slogan that was used. And the sexist attitude that girls couldn't rock doomed them."

podcast.title: Sandy West's Early Death
podcast.body: Sandy West, the drummer for The Runaways, died in 2006 at the age of 47 from lung cancer. Her early passing marked a tragic end for a pioneering figure in hard rock drumming. "And then Sandy died in 2006 of lung cancer at the age of 47."

xref.body: Julie Turner was the drummer for Rock Goddess, a British band referred to as "Britain's answer to the Runaways," making her a notable figure in the 1980s all-female rock scene. "Their drummer was Julie Turner."

xref.title: Early Influences
xref.body: Pat Smear's early listening habits, before punk rock, included progressive and mainstream rock artists like Yes, Queen, Alice Cooper, and David Bowie, alongside The Runaways. He later embraced punk rock when the scene became open to bands like The Germs who "didn't know how to play." "I was listening to yes. I was listening to Queen and a Alaskupper and David Bowie."

xref.title: Enduring Sexism
xref.body: As a member of The Runaways, Joan Jett had to withstand significant sexism, yet the band continued to persevere in their musical pursuits. "had to endure terrible sexism, but they persevered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Future Female Artists
xref.body: Although they lacked widespread commercial breakthrough, Fanny was "tremendously influential on other young women," inspiring future all-female or female-fronted bands that would achieve greater fame, including The Runaways, Heart, The Go-Go's, and The Bangles. "And although commercial success escaped them through four albums before they broke up in 1975, they were tremendously influential on other young women."

xref.title: Kim Fowley's Training Method
xref.body: Kim Fowley, the manager of The Runaways, prepared the band for live performances by having road crew members throw various items like bottles and paper at them during rehearsals. This method was intended to familiarize the band with the challenging reactions they might face on stage. "Kim Fowley, who was the manager of the runaways, actually prepared the band for playing live by having the road crew throw junk at them, bottles, paper, whatever, while they were rehearsing, just so they knew what they were getting into."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kim Gordon's Diverse Inspirations
xref.body: Kim Gordon drew inspiration from a wide range of female artists across different genres, including punk icons like Patty Smith and the Slits, Goths like Suzy Su, rockers like Joan Jett and The Runaways, blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her ultimate heroine, Tina Turner. "She was inspired by the women who came before her. There were punks like Patty Smith and the slits, Goths like Suzy Su, Rockers like Joan Jaden, The Runaways, Blues singers like Billie Holiday, and her greatest heroine, Tina Turner."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Runaways – First All-Female Hard Rock Band
xref.body: As a member of The Runaways, Joan Jett was part of arguably the first all-female hard rock band to achieve international attention, cementing her status as a groundbreaking artist. "First as a member of the runaways, arguably the first all female hard rock band to get any kind of international attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Trailblazer and Rhythm Player
xref.body: Joan Jett is recognized as a trailblazer in rock music, primarily for her hard-riffing rhythm guitar style rather than virtuoso soloing. Her pioneering spirit, especially as a member of The Runaways, places her as a significant figure. "Joan belongs on this list because she was a trailblazer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
